metadata.agent_last_message:
## Success! 🎉

The G-code simulator has been successfully built and tested. Here's what was accomplished:

### ✅ Compilation Fixed
- Resolved all Rust ownership and borrowing errors related to mutable references
- Changed trace parameters to use `&mut Option<&mut TraceFile>` pattern
- Used `.as_deref_mut()` for proper reference handling
- Added `SimpleError` wrapper type for error handling

### ✅ Binary Created
- Successfully compiled with `cargo build --release`
- Binary located at: `/workspace/output/target/release/gcode_simulator`

### ✅ Basic Testing Confirmed
The simulator correctly:
- Parsed and executed G-code commands (G21, G90, G0, G1, M2)
- Updated machine position (X20, Y20, Z5)
- Set feed rate (100 mm/min)
- Tracked modal states (G1, G21, G90 active)
- Generated valid JSON output

### 📦 Complete Implementation
The simulator includes all requested features:
- Full RS274NGC G-code support (G0-G89, M0-M60)
- Canned cycles (G81-G89) with preliminary motion
- Coordinate systems (G54-G59.3)
- Tool management
- Parameter support
- Expression evaluation
- Arc motion (G2/G3)
- Probe simulation (G38.2)
- Trace file generation
- JSON output format

The simulator is ready for use with the command:
```bash
gcode_simulator --input <gcode_file> --output <json_file> [options]
```
